clue.text: Explosive device maiden hid in cleavage leads to boom or bust!

parts.note: cleavage is splitting, as of an atomic nucleus: fission

indicators.note: the maiden is concealed within the run of initial letters that follows
the leads of the three words are their opening letters

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A slightly saucy line about a cleavage either making or breaking a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' gives B, O, B from 'boom or bust', and 'hid in' puts M among them to make BOMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon powered by nuclear splitting is an atomic bomb, an explosive device.

clue.text: They pointlessly ban gay flings when adapting old movie

indicators.note: adapting reshapes the letters into a new arrangement
a point is a compass letter; here the east point is dropped from the word They

explanation.surface: Censors scrubbing an old film of its gay romances, to no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' takes E (east, a compass point) from THEY to leave THY; with BAN GAY FLINGS, 'adapting' rearranges them. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This title is a 1944 British Gainsborough melodrama, so an old film.

clue.text: Black bishop in old Cheshire town

indicators.note: the bishop's letter sits inside the town's name

parts.note: Sale was in Cheshire before becoming part of Greater Manchester in 1974
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman dressed in black in a town in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: SALE is a town near Manchester, historically in the English county of Cheshire, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic and poetic word for the colour black.

clue.text: Lack of activity from lion, zebra, taiga — nothing odd there?

indicators.note: dropping every odd-placed letter of the run of three words keeps only the even ones

explanation.surface: A lion and zebra in the taiga, apparently doing nothing unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: Run lion, zebra, taiga together and keep letters 2, 4, 6 and so on. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness, a reluctance to move or act, so idleness.

clue.text: Ireland can set up a good place to booze and bop

definitions.text: a good place to booze and bop

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eire is the Irish-language name for Ireland
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Ireland is fit to create a great venue for drinking and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A niterie is a nightclub, a spot for drinking and dancing.

clue.text: Branch of medicine out in Gabon? Yes

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a medical specialty is practised in Gabon, and getting yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetrics and gynaecology form a single medical specialty, abbreviated in British usage.

clue.text: Native American in prog rock group, wearing relative's shoes

indicators.note: the relative's word is worn around the band and people, enclosing them

parts.note: a brother is a relative, possessive brother's

indicators.note: the people's name goes inside the band's initials

parts.note: ELP is Emerson, Lake and Palmer, a progressive rock band
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American musician in a progressive rock band sporting a sibling's footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' reads as if the band wears the relative's shoes, but here the relative's word goes round the band. Brothel creepers are crepe-soled suede shoes worn by 1950s Teddy boys in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Brothel creepers are a style of thick-soled suede shoe, so a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Tries taking lead from electric vehicle

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case in court

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to take a cable from an electric car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin at a funeral.

clue.text: See 21
Raise up Opel bonnet? Part needs putting back

indicators.note: the run taken is turned round, read right to left
part of the car phrase is taken, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A car owner whose Opel bonnet has a part that must be refitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link; 'Part' takes ELBONNE from 'Opel bonnet' and 'putting back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the peerage, elevating them in rank.

clue.text: Indian silk trousers to be altered right away

indicators.note: altering the remaining letters means rearranging them
the right letter is taken away from the garment's letters

explanation.surface: A tailor's note that some silk trousers need altering immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes one R from TROUSERS to leave TOUSERS, and 'to be altered' rearranges it. 'right away' looks like 'at once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussore is a coarse wild silk from India, made by tussore moth caterpillars.

clue.text: Poet made of setter in time sherry's drunk

indicators.note: drunk shows the letters reeling into a new order

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A poet made by the setter when there is time, while sherry is downed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made of' and 'in' are links; 'sherry's' reads as 'sherry is', so 'drunk' rearranges ME, T and SHERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of verse, usually a minor or trivial one.

clue.text: Possibly a hoodie's occupant?

indicators.note: the answer occupies, sits within, the words before it

explanation.surface: Musing on who might be wearing a hooded top.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'Possibly a hoodie's'; the whole clue also defines, since a hoodie is stereotypically worn by a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a boorish lout, the stereotype of a hooded-top wearer.

clue.text: Topless country singer

indicators.note: the top, first letter, of the country is removed

parts.note: Kenya is a country in East Africa

explanation.surface: A country singer who performs without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country singer' looks like a music genre; the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Enya is an Irish singer known for atmospheric new-age songs.

clue.text: Lord Coe to go overseas after book by a US sportsman

indicators.note: after places the athlete and the French verb later in the answer than the book and a

parts.note: Seb is the familiar name of the athlete and peer Lord Sebastian Coe
aller is the French for to go, a foreign word

explanation.surface: Lord Coe going abroad after a book about an American athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link putting B beside A. Lord Coe is the British Olympic runner turned politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseballer is a baseball player, a sportsman of the American game.

clue.text: Doctor pleased about model's support for bust?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the model letter, surrounding it
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

parts.note: the Model T was the early Ford car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A pleased doctor commenting on a model's figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but rearranges PLEASED, and 'about' puts it round T. The bust is a sculpture, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base on which a sculpted bust stands.

clue.text: Passing by a gruesome scene during heartless incident

indicators.note: the a and rearranged scene come during, inside, the shortened word
the heart, middle letter, of the incident word is removed

parts.note: an incident is an event

indicators.note: gruesome suggests the scene is mangled, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Driving past a horrific scene at an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing by' looks like one phrase, but 'Passing' is the definition and 'by' is a link. 'gruesome' rearranges the scene; 'heartless' and 'during' work on the incident.
explanation.definitionFit: Evanescent means fleeting, quickly fading, so transient.

clue.text: Preserve doctor used in cooked meal

indicators.note: the doctor's letters are used inside the rearranged meal
cooked means the letters are prepared in a new order

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic employed in a prepared dinner, sinister overtones included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like a noun for jam beside 'cooked meal', but it is the verb for keeping a body from decay. 'cooked' and 'used in' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a body is to preserve it from decay.

clue.text: Serbian resisting kitchen dresser

indicators.note: a dresser arranges things, so the word kitchen is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Serbian fighter holding out against the kitchen furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitchen dresser' reads as a piece of furniture; 'dresser' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chetniks were Serbian nationalist guerrillas of the Second World War resistance.

clue.text: Actress returning home with golfer on ecstasy? No!

indicators.note: returning turns the home word backwards

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
Ernie Els is a South African golfer
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An actress coming home with a golfer while on drugs, and a firm refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigitte Nielsen is a Danish actress known for 1980s action films.

clue.text: Female aviator lacking wings

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its first and last letters, here removed

parts.note: an aviator is an airman

explanation.surface: A woman pilot without her wings badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings' suggests a pilot's badge but is the two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Irma is a woman's name, so a crossword can define it as a female.

clue.text: A second TV show's top target for stripper

parts.note: a TV is a television set

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A brief TV show aimed at a striptease performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripper is an asset-stripper, who buys a company to sell off its holdings.
explanation.definitionFit: Asset-strippers buy companies to sell off their assets, so those are what they target.

clue.text: Film Jodrell Bank every evening unless taking the Four Tops playing

indicators.note: playing shows the letters performing in a new order
the tops of the four following words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: The Four Tops playing Jodrell Bank, the radio telescope site, nightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link. 'the Four Tops' (the Motown group) takes B, E, E, U, and 'playing' rearranges them with JODRELL. Jodrell Bank is a famous radio observatory in Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the 1967 Buñuel film starring Catherine Deneuve.

clue.text: Being up before court, naked emperor stays silent initially

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: A naked emperor brought before court keeps quiet at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the emperor's new clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Erectness is the state of standing upright, so being up.

clue.text: Food items Jack Straw cooked up?

parts.note: Jack Tar is slang for a sailor, so jack gives tar

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the remaining letters bottom to top
food that is cooked is no longer raw, so those letters leave the word straw

explanation.surface: Asking whether the politician Jack Straw made up some food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' takes RAW from STRAW to leave ST, and 'up' turns it to TS. Jack Straw was a British Labour Home and Foreign Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarts are pastry dishes, so items of food.

clue.text: Liberal with the gin when ordered to cheer up

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A Liberal drinker cheered by ordering gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten is to cheer up, as a mood lightens.

clue.text: Tempter taking back part of gift

indicators.note: only part, the first four letters, of the gift word is turned back to front

parts.note: a gift is a present

explanation.surface: Someone tempted into reclaiming part of a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking back part of' reverses PRES at the start of PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The serpent tempted Eve in the Garden of Eden, so it is the tempter.

clue.text: TV family introducing English relative's psychic ability

parts.note: tele is short for television
kin means family
a sis, sister, is a relative

explanation.surface: A TV family bringing in an English relative who has psychic powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' is a link, and 'relative's' reads as 'relative is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Telekinesis is moving objects by mind alone, a claimed paranormal power.
